instruction: Make an order for as many things as possible with $600 from my amazon wishlist.
notes: Task is 'order as many wish-list items as possible within $600'. Modeled as greedy cheapest-first selection: product-k placeholders are bound at runtime to the k-th cheapest wish-list entries whose cumulative price (plus delivery fee, since the order's paid_amount must be <= 600) stays within budget; each is moved from the wish list to the cart with quantity 1 (evaluation requires ordered_quantity == 1 and WishListEntry changes, hence move_product_from_wish_list_to_cart rather than add_product_to_cart). The number of affordable items is unknown a priori; the problem uses 5 placeholders and a count chain (count-0..count-5 via succ) with (max-count-within-budget count-5 budget-600) so place_order is only enabled once all selected items are in the cart; adjust the number of product objects/count objects to the real wish list. clear_cart is done first so no pre-existing cart items (not from the wish list) end up in the order (CartEntry changes are ignored by evaluation). Payment card and address ids are discovered via show_payment_cards/show_addresses (known-id); addresses must not be modified. complete_task takes no answer. Reference plan has 13 calls.
